title: Sol‐Gel Coupled KOH Activation Synthesis of Lignin‐Derived Hierarchical Porous Carbon: Optimization and Supercapacitor Applications
abstract: Abstract Porous carbon derived from lignin has attracted significant interest due to its potential application in supercapacitors. In this work, lignin‐derived hierarchical porous carbons (LHPCs) with tunable surface areas and pore size distributions were synthesized via a sol‐gel process coupled with KOH activation. A hydrogel was first formed by chemically crosslinking lignin with resorcinol and subsequently freeze‐dried to obtain a porous aerogel precursor. The LHPCs were synthesized by carbonization and KOH activation of the aerogel precursor. The influence of activation parameters on the microstructure and capacitive performance of LHPCs was systematically investigated. Characterization results revealed that the LHPCs possessed an interconnected hierarchical porous structure with a low degree of graphitization. The optimal sample, LHPC 700‐3 , exhibited a surface area of 2117.3 m 2 g −1 , a total pore volume of 1.57 cm 3 g −1 , and a micropore volume of 0.86 cm 3 g −1 . As a supercapacitor electrode material, LHPC 700‐3 exhibited a high specific capacitance of 228 F g −1 and an energy density of 7.9 Wh kg −1 at 125 W kg −1 . Furthermore, it exhibited excellent cycling stability, retaining 97.6% of its initial capacitance after 10,000 charge/discharge cycles at 20 A g −1 . This study presents a promising strategy for transforming lignin into economical, high‐performance electrode materials for supercapacitors.
